text:
sara: FYI — Acme Prod complaining of sustained throughput drop on their Dedicated pool since ~00:12 UTC. 30% fewer tokens/sec, tail latency up to 1.2s, intermittent 429s. Traces show a ton of tiny batches (1-4 tokens). Can runtime team take a look?

support-agent: Customer workload switched to lots of short prompts (avg seq len ~10). Customer request id: r-01AZX. No billing anomalies. Here's a curl they used to repro: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' -d '{\"prompt\":\"hey\"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`

ben: Ack. Can you paste a few examples of batch metrics and autoscaler events? My gut: continuous batcher warming or scheduler quantum is creating micro-batches. Also check max_batch_tokens and batch_window_ms.

chris: Pasted relevant config from the dedicated pool (anonymized):
```
pool: dedicated-eu-4
batch_window_ms: 1
max_batch_tokens: 128
scheduler_quantum_us: 1000
```
And latest metrics (scraped at 00:20 UTC):
`batch_size_count{pool=\"dedicated-eu-4\",size=\"1\"} 12488`
`batch_size_count{pool=\"dedicated-eu-4\",size=\"2\"} 534`
`batch_size_count{pool=\"dedicated-eu-4\",size=\">=8\"} 12`
So yeah, overwhelmingly size=1. Autoscaler events show scale up started at 00:14 but node join completed at 00:16 (≈120s delay).`

support-agent: Customer says their QPS is steady (180 qps) but average tokens/request dropped, so we expect smaller batches but not this extreme. They saw the drop right after a deploy at 23:58.

ben: Two hypotheses: 1) batch_window_ms = 1ms effectively disables batching for short requests — quantum mismatch. 2) continuous-batcher prefill/prefix caching didn't warm because KV cache was invalidated after deploy, so every request triggers cold path and small micro-batches. Quick test: bump batch_window_ms to 8-10ms on a canary and see batch size distribution.

chris: Uploading autoscaler log snippet: `autoscaler: triggering_scale_up reason=queue_depth>threshold target=+2 nodes; t0=00:14:05; node_registration_delay=120000ms`. infra-bot also shows GC spikes on one host around 00:13 which may have delayed joining.

lee: Repro steps I'm going to run locally against a canary pool: `python tools/loadgen.py --qps 200 --prompt \"hi\" --seq_len 8 --duration 300` and check `/metrics` for batch_size_count. If we reproduce, I'll roll the batch_window change to 10ms for canary.

ben: Quick quick check you can run without cluster:
```
# simulate many short requests
wrk -t12 -c200 -d60s --script=short_prompt.lua https://dedicated-canary.redwood/api
```
Then watch `batch_size_count` and `inflight_batches`. If most batches=1 we know it's window/quantum.

chris: Temporary mitigation options: 1) route this customer to a spare pool where batch_window_ms was 8ms; 2) enable request coalescing at the API gateway for short requests (cheap flag flip); 3) apply canary change to batch_window_ms=10ms + bump max_batch_tokens to 256 to allow more aggregation. I prefer 3 for minimal disruption.

support-agent: Customer agreed to a short maintenance window at 01:30 UTC for a canary config change and wants us to monitor closely. They asked for ETA to resolve.

ben: Plan: 1) deploy canary config to 5% of the pool at 01:30; 2) monitor `batch_size_count`, `tokens_per_second`, `p99_latency`, and `429_rate` for 15m; 3) if improvement >15% tokens/sec and p99 drops, rollout to remaining nodes. Rollback plan: revert config and route traffic to spare pool. I'll own the rollout.

lee: I'm executing the loadgen now and can confirm local repro: with batch_window_ms=1ms `batch_size_count size=1` ~85% of batches. With a local change to 8ms it drops to ~22% and size>=8 increases.

infra-bot: autoscaler: scale_event { \"pool\": \"dedicated-eu-4\", \"action\": \"scale_up\", \"delta\": 2, \"start\": 00:14:05, \"completed\": 00:16:05 }

chris: I'll prepare the canary patch: increase batch_window_ms=10, max_batch_tokens=256, enable prefill=true. Pushing to canary at 01:30 UTC. Also adding a guard: if 429_rate > 1% then automatic rollback.

support-agent: Customer notified. They appreciate the quick response.

sara: Thanks all — leaving open until the canary verifies. I'll ping @support-agent once we have customer confirmation. :eyes:
